source.title_on_document: The Use of Prompt Engineering in ChatGPT to Improve the Ability to Write Ethnoliteracy-Based Fiction Stories in Elementary Schools: A Quasi-Experimental Study

paper_design_summary: The paper reports 50 fifth-grade students in two nonequivalent classes of 25 at a public elementary school in Cimahi, Indonesia: one received ethnoliteracy-based fiction-writing lessons with structured ChatGPT prompting, and the other received conventional lessons without AI; analyzed counts are not separately stated (p. 809, PDF p. 6). Both classes were administered fiction-writing pretests and posttests using an eight-indicator rubric covering structure, plot cohesion, setting, characters, message, creativity of language style, local cultural values, and spelling (pp. 809-813, PDF pp. 6-10). Results include indicator means, N-gains, and an ambiguously identified t-test in Table 8, labeled Reading Comprehension; its precise outcome, timepoint, and choice between paired and independent tests are unconfirmed (pp. 811-815, PDF pp. 8-12).

outcomes.name: Reported t-test discussed as fiction-writing skills (Table 8: 'Reading Comprehension'; outcome/timepoint unclear)
outcomes.measure_detail: A fiction-writing assessment rubric was used; three experts validated the instruments, but the identity and expertise of the people or system scoring the stories are not stated (p. 810, PDF p. 7; pp. 811-814, PDF pp. 8-11). Table 8 is not clearly identified as an aggregate of this rubric; its exact outcome, analysis unit, and timepoint remain unresolved (p. 815, PDF p. 12).

contrasts.reported: Table 8 labels its variable 'Reading Comprehension' and prints Thitung = -0.538, Df = 50, sig (2-tailed) = 0.593, and 'H0 is accepted'. The preceding paragraph instead prints 0.0593, says 'Ha is accepted', and claims a significant effect. The following paragraph calls the test one-tailed and states that there is no significant difference in fiction-writing skills between the ChatGPT and conventional classes. The methods mention both Paired Sample T-Test and Independent Sample T-Test; Table 8 does not specify which was used, its timepoint, or whether the variable is an overall writing-rubric score. Arm names and comparison_type describe the class comparison discussed in the surrounding prose, and direction describes only the printed Table 8 conclusion. Separately, p. 814 reports N-gain = 0.069 for the experimental class and 0.062 for the control class, both 'low category'; these are not standardized treatment effects.
contrasts.locator: p. 815 (PDF p. 12), Table 8 and immediately preceding/following paragraphs; p. 811 (PDF p. 8), Data Analysis Techniques; p. 814 (PDF p. 11), N-gain paragraph

eligibility.reason: The two classes were compared under a nonequivalent control group design explicitly without randomization (p. 808, PDF p. 5, Research design), with purposive sampling (p. 809, PDF p. 6, Research participants), so criterion 1 is not met and core eligibility remains no. The reported sample is exactly 50 students, 25 per group, but posttest completion, exclusions, and analyzed counts are not separately reported; criterion 2 is therefore unclear (p. 809, PDF p. 6; pp. 812-815, PDF pp. 9-12, results tables). Written stories receive rubric scores including creativity of language style, supporting criterion 3 (pp. 811-813, PDF pp. 8-10, rubric and Tables 3 and 5). Scorer identity is not established by instrument validation (p. 810, PDF p. 7). AI availability during posttest writing is unstated, so with_ai versus after_ai remains unresolved (p. 809, PDF p. 6, Research Procedures; p. 813, PDF p. 10, paragraph before Table 5). The conflicting labeling and significance claims around Table 8 do not establish its exact outcome or timepoint (p. 815, PDF p. 12).

one_line_finding: Table 8 ('Reading Comprehension'; p. 815, PDF p. 12) prints t = -0.538, df = 50 and sig (2-tailed) = 0.593 ('H0 is accepted') with unresolved outcome/timepoint and contradictory preceding prose (0.0593; 'Ha is accepted'), while experimental/control posttest means are 52/49 for language-style creativity and 60/38 for local cultural values (Table 5, pp. 813-814, PDF pp. 10-11), and N-gain is 0.069/0.062 (p. 814, PDF p. 11).
open_questions: How many students in each class completed the posttest and entered each analysis? The paper reports a research sample of 50 students, 25 per class, but no separate analyzed counts or attrition information (p. 809, PDF p. 6; pp. 812-815, PDF pp. 9-12, results tables); Table 8 df = 50 does not resolve this.

Who or what scored the stories, and what was the scorer expertise? Three experts validated the instruments, but the story scorers are not identified (p. 810, PDF p. 7, Instrument data validation; pp. 811-814, PDF pp. 8-11, rubric and results).

Was ChatGPT available while the scored posttest stories were written? The procedures separate AI-supported lessons from the posttest, and 'assessed using ChatGPT engineering prompts' does not establish AI access during production (p. 809, PDF p. 6, Research Procedures; p. 813, PDF p. 10, paragraph before Table 5).

What outcome, timepoint, analysis unit, and exact contrast does Table 8 test, and is the test paired or independent, one-tailed or two-tailed? The methods mention both paired and independent tests, the table labels the outcome 'Reading Comprehension' with sig (2-tailed) = 0.593 and 'H0 is accepted', the preceding prose prints 0.0593 and says 'Ha is accepted', and the following prose describes a one-tailed test with no significant class difference (p. 811, PDF p. 8; p. 815, PDF p. 12).
notes: Story structure, plot cohesion, setting, characterization, and message are retained as narrative-quality outcomes under the codebook's usefulness construct. Spelling (indicator 8) is omitted from the creativity outcome list as a technical writing measure: its rubric concerns sentence structure and spelling conforming to EYD (p. 812, PDF p. 9, Table 3; p. 814, PDF p. 11, Table 5 continuation). For indicator comparisons, statistics_available = ['none'] means none of the listed summaries with dispersion, analyzed counts, or inferential information is supplied; descriptive arm means are recorded in reported, since the vocabulary has no means-only option. treatment_higher records descriptive posttest means and does not assert statistical significance. No effect sizes were computed. The full markdown was read through the references; the PDF ends with references and identifies no appendix or supplement.
